label: Remote onboarding
summary: Remote onboarding is the process of settling into a new job or contract assignment without physical presence in an office. In Maaike's work, it is treated as a harder variant of regular onboarding because it strips away the ambient, informal affordances that help a new person orient and connect. The core challenge is social: how do you meet people and build rapport when all you have is a digital channel?
how_maaike_uses: Maaike approaches remote onboarding as a practical problem she has had to solve repeatedly across 20+ years of starting new roles and 4+ years of contracting. She frames the absence of casual office moments as a missing contextual community and compensates with deliberate tactics: a self-organised onboarding tour where each person recommends two more contacts, and a short joint online tea break to build informal rapport. She also explicitly addresses employers and contractors, telling them to over-communicate because new remote colleagues are entering what she calls a black box, with few affordances to lean on.
open_questions: The checklist Maaike references is presented as a living document she invites others to contribute to, so which items are still missing from it is left open.
The relationship between building communities and easing remote onboarding is gestured at across both posts but never fully worked out.
